messages:
sam: FYI - we're seeing sustained GPU clock drops on a subset of hosted-eu1 hosts. Tail latency for 13B and larger models climbed ~3-4x starting ~08:10 UTC.

vendor-alert-bot: Alert: HW_THERMAL_THROTTLE detected on rack eu1-gpu-rack-7. Sensor stream: https://infra.redwood.ai/alerts/3187654321 :rotating_light:

lucy: Oncall taking. Initial check - GPU telemetry shows thermal events and auto-throttle engaged. Could be datacenter cooling pressure after maintenance. Engaging live-migration for hot tenants off affected hosts.

support: Support queue seeing chat errors and elevated latency reports. Draft external line: "We're investigating increased latency for larger models in EU-West. Mitigation underway: tenant migration and throttles. No customer data loss expected." Approve?

sam: Approve. Also add note that we're working with colo on cooling/CRAC reset.

ops-bot: Live-migration plan: evacuate 25% of pods from eu1-gpu-rack-7 -> eu1-gpu-rack-3 over 10min waves. Starting wave 1 now.

lucy: Wave 1 migration done @3187654400 - migrated 8 tenants, observed latency improve on those flows. Continuing waves.

vendor-alert-bot: Vendor update: colo acknowledged elevated inlet temp, techs en route to inspect CRAC unit. ETA 25-35 minutes.

support: Posted status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INCIDENT-2026-0901-09  Mitigations: tenant migrations, temporary capacity shift. Will update in 20m.

sam: Current impact: ~10 customers with >2x tail latency intermittently; 2 customers on large-context endpoints are seeing degraded UX. We're prioritizing them for migration.

lucy: If vendor can't stabilize, fallback is to cordon rack and drain remaining pods to spare capacity in eu1 and eu2. That will cause short rolling failovers but should restore latency.

incident-bot: Monitoring window started for post-migration metrics. Postmortem tags: "hw-thermal", "rack-evacuations", "colo-ops".

sam: Thanks team. I'll keep driving migrations and update support after next wave. Ping me for escalations. :thumbsup:
